title: continuous-batcher-scheduler-tuning-queueing-fairness-starvation-timeouts
author: Jordan Alvarez
body: Motivation: production workloads showed intermittent p99 latency spikes under mixed-size request distributions. Root cause analysis pointed to queuing imbalance in the continuous batcher scheduler where long-running large-sequence requests could cause starvation of small low-latency requests, and timeouts were not consistently enforced across backpressure paths. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention heuristics, and tighten timeout handling. Changes: 1) Implemented a weighted-queue policy that classifies requests by estimated token length and assigns dynamic weights to ensure small requests get prioritized when latency SLOs are close to violation. 2) Added starvation prevention counters and a backoff window so requests waiting beyond a threshold are temporarily boosted to avoid indefinite queueing behind large batches. 3) Tightened bundle assembly timeouts and made the timeout configuration pluggable with defaults tuned for typical low-latency routes. 4) Improved KV-cache interaction: when a request is boosted it re-evaluates cached prefixes to reduce recomputation and avoid cache thrashing. 5) Added telemetry: per-class queue depth, boost events, timeout hits, and preemption counts. Benchmarks: internal perf runs on c7i.8x and a mixed workload (60% short <64 tokens, 30% medium 64-512, 10% long >512) show 8-12% reduction in median latency and 15-22% reduction in p99 latency for short/medium requests under load, with overall throughput unchanged. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind continuous-batcher.scheduler_v2 and staged in Dedicated clusters for 48h canary, monitor queueing metrics and latency SLOs, then roll to hosted after verification. Testing: unit tests for queueing rules and starvation counters, integration tests against the runtime harness including simulated long-running requests, and load tests that reproduce prior spike. Notes: this PR intentionally does not change kernel selection logic; follow-up will evaluate combining scheduling signals with kernel latency models. See linked Linear tasks ENG-1123 and ENG-1187 for follow-ups and tuning matrix.

review_comments: Avery Chen: Could you explain the choice of default boost window (250ms) and how sensitive it is on 8x GPU hosts?

Jordan Alvarez (author): The 250ms default was chosen based on empirical runs in ENG-1123; we added a knob so Dedicated customers can tune. I added a comment and unit test showing behavior at 100/250/500ms in the test harness.
Priya Nair: I'm concerned about preemption causing wasted work for large batches; do we have metrics to track recomputation?
Jordan Alvarez (author): Yes, added preemption_count and recompute_hits metrics, and updated perf numbers — recompute overhead measured <3% for mixed workloads in our canary.
Marcus Lee: CI flake on scheduler_end_to_end_test.py, appears unrelated (test harness timing). Can we stabilize?
Jordan Alvarez (author): Pushed a follow-up to increase harness timeout and reran CI; tests are stable now.
Avery Chen: Approved after CI green and verifying telemetry in canary cluster.
Priya Nair: LGTM, left a minor doc suggestion which I will follow up on.
release_notes: Scheduler: improved continuous-batcher fairness and starvation prevention; default boost window=250ms; added metrics (queue_depth_per_class, boost_events, preemption_count, timeout_hits); feature-flagged rollout.
